Jordan: Hi all 1 I'm on my first overnight on-call shift and ran into a couple of blockers. VPN won't connect (timeout) and I can't assume the prod-k8s role to run kubectl. Any quick help?
Ava: Welcome to night shifts! Quick checks: are you on the corp VPN (Cisco AnyConnect) or the new wireguard client? We migrated last month. Also confirm you're in the `oncall-aws` IAM group.
Jordan: Using AnyConnect. I saw the email about wireguard but didn't switch yet. How do I check the IAM group?
Devon: Easiest: run `aws sts get-caller-identity` and then `idp-cli whoami` (internal tool) to show your groups. If you don't have oncall-aws, ping @infra. I'll add you if Ava can't.
Jordan: `aws sts` works but idp-cli fails with `AccessDenied`.
Ava: That means you don't have the SAML assertion mapping. @Devon can add you. Meanwhile, for quick triage we can give you read-only kube access: `kubectl --context=prod-monitor get pods -n redwood` (we've got a read-only role bound). Use the `KUBECONFIG=/etc/redwood/oncall/kubeconfig` path.
Jordan: I don't have that kubeconfig locally. How do I get it on my laptop?
Devon: Copy it from the secure bucket: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-infra/oncall/kubeconfigs/prod-monitor ~/.kube/prod-monitor --profile oncall-temp` then export KUBECONFIG. I'll DM you the temp creds.
infra-bot: INFO: Temporary credentials issued for jordan, valid 2h. Follow company security guidelines.
Jordan: Thanks, creds worked and I can list pods now. Second issue: PagerDuty push shows but tapping doesn't ack. It flashes 'processing'.
Ava: Known PD iOS bug sometimes when tethered to corporate VPN. Try toggling airplane mode then ack, or use web PD: `https://redwood.pagerduty.com` and ack there. Also verify PD mobile version >= 8.2.
Jordan: Web ack worked. I tried to run the standard triage flow on svc-rate-limiter alert but the runbook link in PD 404s.
Devon: Ah, that's the new repo location. Runbook moved from Confluence to GitHub docs last week. New path: `https://github.com/redwood-infra/runbooks/blob/main/svc-rate-limiter.md`. We should update PD.
Ava: Quick triage snippet from the runbook: `kubectl logs -n redwood -l app=rate-limiter --tail=200`, check `redis-cluster` latency `redis-cli --latency -h <host>`. If service errors >5% over 10m, flip the feature flag to degrade to safe-mode: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/toggle -d 'svc=rate-limiter&mode=safe'`.
Jordan: Did that, saw errors dropping after safe-mode. Should I open an incident?
Ava: For now open a P1 incident if user-facing degradation >10% or multiple downstream services impacted. Otherwise file an Ops ticket and note the mitigation in PD. Post a short thread in #incidents with summary and whether we need on-call followup.
Jordan: Creating incident now. Quick Q: who needs to be looped in for the follow-up RCA? Product + SRE?
Devon: Include the service owner (check OWNERS.md), SRE lead, and the Product PM. Use the postmortem template in the repo `docs/postmortem-template.md`. Keep it action-oriented.
oncall-bot: Reminder: New oncallers should schedule two shadow sessions within your first month. Run `/shadow-request @ava` to book.
Jordan: One last nit: noisy alert spam from `svc-rate-limiter` during deploys. Can we mute deploy-time alerts?
Ava: We usually add a suppression window in PD for deploy job names (CI -> deploy-*). For immediate fix, set alert suppression for 30m in PD under the alert rule. For longer term, open an ops-automation ticket to add a deploy label exclusion.
Jordan: Awesome, thanks for the rapid help. I'll finish the incident writeup and schedule the shadow. Appreciated :thumbsup:
Ava: Happy to help. Ping if anything else pops up. Good first night!
